fit: orange item and Rome III constipation in Brazilian older adults
assessment: Constipation was reported in 31/120 consumers versus 9/19 nonconsumers (unadjusted p=.054). The survey gives no confirmed raw preparation, adjusted effect, severity change or separate Parkinson cohort.

fit: pasteurized orange juice and a bowel diary in ten healthy women
assessment: The baseline and day-60 ordinal frequency scores were 1.40 and 1.40. The reported diary comparisons were inconclusive across periods. A sequential design without a concurrent group cannot isolate the juice effect.

fit: Spanish sage essential oil and acute task fatigue in healthy adults
assessment: Planned comparisons after the single-dose crossover found less task fatigue on three of six repetitions at one hour and five of six at four hours. The species, oil and outcome differ from fresh culinary sage and Parkinson fatigue.

fit: independent combined flaxseed-derived omega-3 and vitamin E trial in Parkinson disease
assessment: Part III mean changes were −1.9 and +3.1, with p=.05 as printed and no clear part-level benefit in the authors’ interpretation. No separate rigidity, verified oil pressing or oil-only estimate.

fit: acute oral caffeine and coffee perception in tremor
assessment: Six percent of the Parkinson survey group perceived worse tremor after coffee. The author abstract gives no increase after one 325 mg caffeine dose in a separate short test and no rest-tremor-specific estimate. Original full report remains open.

fit: peppermint extract and tail-suspension immobility in male mice
assessment: Peppermint extract plus rotenone produced 183.67 seconds mean immobility versus 251.48 with rotenone alone (p<.001). The same animals improved locomotion. This is a different species, extract, animal assay and exposure from fresh spearmint in people.
